import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import statsmodels.api as sm
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Load data and select relevant columns
df = pd.read_csv('reef.csv', usecols=['id_reef', 'depth', 'biomass', 'turnover'])
# Drop any missing values (should be none for these cols)
df = df.dropna(subset=['biomass', 'turnover', 'depth', 'id_reef'])

# 2. Ensure depth is categorical
df['depth'] = df['depth'].astype('category')  # Shallow, Deep

# 3. Fit linear mixed‐effects model: turnover ~ biomass + depth + (1|id_reef)
model = smf.mixedlm("turnover ~ biomass + C(depth)", df, groups=df["id_reef"] )
result = model.fit(reml=True)

# 4. Output model coefficients and confidence intervals
print("Mixed‐Effects Model Summary:")
print(result.summary())
print("\n95% Confidence Intervals:")
print(result.conf_int())

# 5. Diagnostic plots
fitted = result.fittedvalues
residuals = result.resid

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5))
# Residuals vs Fitted
axes[0].scatter(fitted, residuals, alpha=0.3)
axes[0].axhline(0, color='red', linestyle='--')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Fitted Values')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Residuals')
axes[0].set_title('Residuals vs Fitted')
# Q-Q Plot
sm.qqplot(residuals, line='45', ax=axes[1])
axes[1].set_title('Normal Q-Q Plot')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 6. Scatterplot of turnover vs biomass colored by depth with fitted lines
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
colors = {'Shallow': 'blue', 'Deep': 'red'}
for d in df['depth'].cat.categories:
    mask = df['depth'] == d
    ax.scatter(df.loc[mask, 'biomass'], df.loc[mask, 'turnover'],
               s=10, alpha=0.3, label=d, color=colors[d])

# Regression lines
x_vals = np.linspace(df['biomass'].min(), df['biomass'].quantile(0.99), 100)
params = result.params
intercept = params['Intercept']
slope = params['biomass']
depth_coef = params.get('C(depth)[T.Deep]', 0.0)
# line for Shallow (baseline)
ax.plot(x_vals, intercept + slope * x_vals, color=colors['Shallow'], linewidth=2)
# line for Deep
ax.plot(x_vals, intercept + depth_coef + slope * x_vals, color=colors['Deep'], linewidth=2)

ax.set_xlabel('Total Biomass (t/ha)')
ax.set_ylabel('Biomass Turnover Rate')
ax.set_title('Turnover vs Biomass by Depth with MixedLM Fits')
ax.legend(title='Depth')
plt.show()

The linear mixed‐effects model (turnover ~ biomass + depth + (1|id_reef)) converged on 137,821 observations (245 reefs). Fixed‐effects estimates (REML):
  • Intercept (Deep baseline at biomass=0): 0.745 (95% CI 0.690 to 0.799), p < 0.001
  • C(depth)[T.Shallow]: +0.183 (95% CI 0.176 to 0.189), p < 0.001
  • biomass: –0.052 per t/ha (95% CI –0.057 to –0.047), p < 0.001
Random intercept variance (id_reef): 0.185.

Diagnostics reveal mild non‐normal residual tails and a negative biomass–turnover trend. Thus, the original hypothesis (deep > shallow turnover) is not supported by this model.
review:
Hypothesis: Deep transects (20 m) exhibit higher biomass turnover rates than shallow transects (5 m), after controlling for biomass.

Implementation: A linear mixed‐effects model was fit to transect‐level data (137,821 observations) with turnover as the response, biomass and a depth factor (Deep baseline; Shallow dummy) as fixed effects, and a random intercept for reef (id_reef). Residual vs. fitted and Q–Q diagnostic plots were generated, along with a scatterplot of turnover vs. biomass colored by depth and overlaid with the model’s fitted lines.

Results: 
• Intercept (Deep at biomass = 0): 0.745 (95% CI 0.690–0.799, p < .001)
• Shallow vs. Deep: +0.183 (95% CI 0.176–0.189, p < .001)
• Biomass effect: –0.052 per t / ha (95% CI –0.057 to –0.047, p < .001)
• Random intercept variance (id_reef): 0.185

The positive Shallow coefficient indicates that, after accounting for biomass, shallow transects have significantly higher turnover than deep transects—i.e., deep transects exhibit lower turnover. The hypothesis (deep > shallow turnover) is therefore not supported. Residual diagnostics show mild non‐normal tails but no major heteroscedasticity. Overall, the experiment was implemented faithfully and the hypothesis was tested rigorously.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Reefs with smaller average fish body size (biomass per individual) exhibit higher production‐to‐biomass (P/B) ratios, controlling for SST and biomass density.

experiment_plan.objective: Test whether mean individual fish size is negatively related to turnover (P/B) rates, indicating that communities dominated by smaller fish have faster biomass turnover.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Compute mean individual size for each transect: size = biomass (kg or t/ha) divided by abundance (fish counts).
2. Calculate P/B ratio for each transect: prod/biomass, filtering out zero‐biomass or zero‐abundance cases.
3. Aggregate to reef‐year‐depth level to obtain mean size, mean P/B, mean_sst, and mean biomass density.
4. Fit a linear mixed‐effects model with mean P/B as response; fixed effects: mean size, mean_sst, mean biomass; random intercepts for id_reef (or region).
5. Check the significance and sign of the mean‐size coefficient; validate model assumptions (residual plots, Q–Q).
6. Optionally include an interaction between mean size and mean_sst to see if the size–P/B relationship changes with temperature variability.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Table of mixed‐model coefficients (especially mean size effect) with confidence intervals.
• Diagnostic plots of residuals vs fitted and normal Q–Q.
• Scatterplot of mean P/B vs mean size colored by mean_sst with fitted regression plane or lines.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: The strength of the negative biomass–turnover relationship has weakened over time (i.e., the community’s compensatory response has changed across decades).

experiment_plan.objective: Determine whether the slope of turnover ~ biomass changes between early and late study periods, indicating temporal shifts in community dynamics.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Define a period factor: e.g., Pre‐2010 vs Post‐2010 (or split at median year).
2. Compute turnover and biomass at transect level (or aggregate to reef‐year‐depth).
3. Fit a linear mixed‐effects model: turnover ~ biomass * period + (1|id_reef).
4. Examine the biomass × period interaction coefficient and its significance to test for slope change.
5. Perform model diagnostics and ensure no violation of homoscedasticity or normality.
6. Visualize turnover vs biomass scatterplots with separate regression lines for each period.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Mixed‐model output showing biomass × period interaction estimate and p‐value.
• Diagnostic plots (residuals vs fitted, Q–Q).
• Overlayed scatterplots of turnover vs biomass with period‐specific fitted lines.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Reefs with greater long‐term SST variability show higher interannual variability in their P/B ratios, indicating that thermal fluctuations drive instability in turnover.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess whether sites experiencing more variable thermal environments have correspondingly more variable biomass turnover between years.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For each id_reef, calculate long‐term SST variability: standard deviation of mean_sst across all years.
2. Compute P/B ratio per reef‐year (aggregated across depths): prod_sum/biomass_sum.
3. For each id_reef calculate interannual P/B variability: standard deviation of reef‐year P/B over time.
4. Fit a linear regression or mixed model: P/B variability ~ SST variability + (1|region).
5. Test significance of SST variability coefficient; check collinearity.
6. Plot P/B variability vs SST variability with regression line.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• Regression table with coefficient for SST variability and confidence intervals.
• Scatterplot of P/B variability vs SST variability colored by region.
• Diagnostic plots for regression assumptions.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Reefs at the northernmost and southernmost latitudes exhibit lower interannual P/B variability than mid‐Gulf reefs, reflecting more stable communities at biogeographic extremes.

experiment_plan.objective: Test whether latitude extremes are associated with reduced turnover variability relative to mid‐latitude reefs.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Compute mean latitude (degree) per reef.
2. Classify reefs into three bins: Lower 20% (south extreme), Middle 60% (mid‐Gulf), Upper 20% (north extreme).
3. Compute interannual P/B variability per reef as above.
4. Compare P/B variability across latitude bins using ANOVA or a mixed model: variability ~ latitude_bin + (1|region).
5. Conduct post‐hoc pairwise tests (Tukey) to see if extremes differ from mid‐Gulf.
6. Check residuals for ANOVA or model diagnostics.
experiment_plan.deliverables:
• ANOVA table or mixed‐model summary with latitude bin effects.
• Boxplots of P/B variability by latitude bin with significance annotations.
• Post‐hoc test results.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: At the reef‐year scale, the absolute difference in P/B between shallow (5 m) and deep (20 m) strata decreases with increasing total reef biomass, implying that high‐biomass reefs have more homogenized turnover across depths.

experiment_plan.objective: Evaluate whether differences in depth‐specific turnover narrow as total biomass increases.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For each reef‐year, aggregate transect data separately for depth = 5 m and 20 m to get mean P/B_shallow and P/B_deep.
2. Compute absolute difference ΔP/B = |P/B_deep – P/B_shallow|.
3. Also aggregate total biomass per reef‐year (sum or mean across depths).
4. Fit a regression or mixed model: ΔP/B ~ total biomass + (1|region).
5. Check coefficient for total biomass (expect negative).
6. Validate assumptions and visualize ΔP/B vs biomass with fitted line.
experiment_plan.deliverables:

• Scatterplot of ΔP/B vs total biomass with regression line.
• Residual diagnostics plots.

untried_experiments.hypothesis: Positive within‐year SST anomalies (relative to long‐term reef mean) are associated with elevated P/B ratios, indicating a compensatory productivity response to thermal stress.

experiment_plan.objective: Test whether “hot” years yield higher turnover per biomass relative to the reef’s background temperature.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For each reef, compute its long‐term mean SST across all years.
2. For each reef‐year, calculate SST anomaly = mean_sst_year – long‐term_mean_sst.
3. Compute reef‐year P/B ratio as prod_sum/biomass_sum.
4. Fit a mixed model: P/B ~ SST_anomaly + mean biomass + (1|id_reef).

experiment_plan.objective: Detect a temporal trend in productivity‐to‐biomass ratios at the regional scale.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. Compute reef‐year P/B ratios per reef as prod_sum/biomass_sum.
2. Fit a linear mixed model: P/B ~ year (continuous) + (1|region).
3. Examine the year coefficient; test if negative and significant.

5. Validate residual assumptions.

experiment_plan.objective: Assess whether within‐region dispersion in productivity rates has contracted, signifying more similar P/B across reefs.
experiment_plan.steps:
1. For each region and year, compute the variance (or standard deviation) of reef‐year P/B across all reefs in that region.
2. Construct a time series of regional P/B variance.

experiment_plan.deliverables:

• Diagnostic plots for model assumptions.
